summary: US-C1: One TTL tier registry - every cached read takes its tier from a single source
description:
**Prefactor for the rest of TKT-31.** "Make the change easy, then make the easy change."

ADR-004 rule 1 says every public read endpoint declares a TTL tiered by data volatility. Today those tiers are string literals scattered across two services - `CacheControlPublicReads`, `CacheControlPublicVenueReads` (catalog), `CacheControlPublicAvailability`, `CacheControlPublicSeatOccupancy` (inventory), `CacheControlPriceResolution` - each correct in isolation, none linked to the tier it claims to be, and nothing able to enumerate which endpoint classes exist.

That is fine while the header is the only artifact. It stops being fine the moment something *caches* on it: US-C2 and US-C3 give the in-memory structures a lifetime, and that lifetime must come from the same value the response header advertises, or cache and contract drift silently and nothing detects it.

Ships a `shared/go/cachetier` package - the ADR-004 tiers named once, each with a `time.Duration` and the exact `Cache-Control` string *derived* from it - and moves catalog's and inventory's emission onto it. **No behaviour change: every emitted header stays byte-identical.**

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] `shared/go/cachetier` defines the ADR-004 tiers (never / seconds / minutes / hours) once. Each carries a `time.Duration` and renders its `Cache-Control` string **from** that duration, so the two cannot disagree.
- [ ] Catalog and inventory public-read handlers emit through the package. Every emitted header byte-identical to today's - proven by the existing tier tests passing **unchanged** (`TestSeatMapReadCacheTierByStatus`, `TestAvailabilityCacheTierIsContractEnforced`, and catalog's public-read tier assertions).
- [ ] A test enumerates every `Cache-Control` value declared in `services/*/api/openapi.yaml` and fails if one is not a tier the registry knows. A future endpoint therefore cannot invent an undeclared tier.
- [ ] The `/openapi.yaml` **spec-document** header (`public, max-age=300`) is explicitly excluded, with the reason in the test: it is a static-asset TTL, not an ADR-004 data tier (ADR-004 amendment TKT-128 says so in as many words).
- [ ] The seat-map `no-store` branch (ADR-004 amendment TKT-107) survives: it is the `never` tier, not an absent one.
- [ ] `make check` green.

Quality gates: `make check`; regenerated code committed before the gate if any spec changes (none expected).

objective.note: One source for a tier's duration and its header string, so a cache built on it in US-C2/C3 cannot drift from the contract.

scope.note: New shared package + catalog/inventory emission + one enumeration test. Explicitly NOT: any caching behaviour, any spec change, any new tier value.

uncertainties.note: None material. Whether the registry keys by endpoint class or by tier alone is a plan-stage call; both satisfy the COS.

dependencies.note: None. First slice of the epic.

approach.note: Constants -> a typed tier with Duration + Header(); the existing named constants become derived values so their call sites and tests are untouched.

success.note: COS are byte-identical headers (existing tests unchanged) plus a new enumeration test that fails on an unknown tier.

binding.rule: Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite). Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

governingAdrs.why: The epic's parent decision. Rule 1 (every public read declares a volatility tier), rule 2 (hot events served from memory, refreshed/invalidated from the write path, write path never served from cache), rule 3 (frontends call-frugal). Its TKT-128 amendment records that rule 2 is accepted and UNIMPLEMENTED and that this epic owns the deployment gap; its TKT-107 amendment splits the seat-map tier on publication status.

Contract-first: a tier that a handler emits must be DECLARED in the service's openapi.yaml or the gate cannot review it. TKT-128 named an emitted-but-undeclared header as a defect in its own right. Any spec edit means regenerating and committing openapi_gen.go BEFORE the gate.

Catalog and inventory wrap responses in contract.ResponseValidator, which validates response HEADERS and fails closed: a Cache-Control value outside the declared enum becomes a 500 with the payload withheld. So the emitted constant and the declaration can only move together.

comments.body:
### Implementation readiness - PASS

Prefactor slice, carved from TKT-31 at decomposition (2026-08-04). Mechanical: it moves five string literals behind one typed tier and adds an enumeration test. No behaviour change is the point, and it is checkable - the existing tier tests must pass unchanged.

`risk:low` claimed: no auth, no money path, no data migration, no CI/deploy config; bounded to one new shared package plus header emission in two services. Restated at claim time per the skill's invariant.

**Claimed** by the agent, first of TKT-31's five children.

**Selection reason:** it is the only child with zero open blockers, and it is the prefactor the other two cache stories depend on - TKT-205 and TKT-206 take their cache lifetime from the registry this ticket creates, so shipping them first would mean writing the lifetime twice and letting the cache and the response header drift.

**Risk verdict: `risk:low` CLAIMED.** Restating why rather than inheriting the label:
- No auth surface, no money path, no data migration, no CI/deploy config.
- No OpenAPI spec change expected, so no `openapi_gen.go` / `api-types.gen.ts` regeneration.
- Behaviour change is *nil* by construction: every emitted `Cache-Control` string must stay byte-identical, and the existing tier tests are the proof - they must pass **unchanged**.
- File count is bounded to one new shared package plus header emission in two services; if the plan comes back needing more than five files, the label comes off and the plan gate returns.

The `risk:low` carve-outs (auth, data migrations, CI/deploy config, >5 files) were each checked, not assumed.

---

**Gates waived for this run.** The repo owner is running TKT-31 and all five children through the pipeline in **fully autonomous mode**, Ready to Done, with all four human gates deliberately waived as a process experiment:
- **Gate 1 (priority)** - given standing; the agent moved the ticket to Ready.
- **Gate 2 (plan approval)** - the agent resolves open decisions itself after the cross-model critique, preferring the critique's recommendation and otherwise the most reversible option. Every self-made decision is recorded in `kind=plan-final`.
- **Gate 3 (review + merge)** - the agent squash-merges after the adversarial ai-review converges, posting the review-guide first as the audit record.
- **Gate 4 (PO acceptance)** - the agent self-validates each COS against test evidence on the merged code.

Everything else in the skill applies unchanged: `config.models` routing with no substitutions, cross-model review for both plan and code, TDD with tests observed red first, `make check` green before every push and after the merge, all marker comments, no AI attribution in commits or PRs.

Branch: `TKT-204-ttl-tier-registry` off `origin/main`.

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (codex companion, `task --effort high`, read-only, 8m22s) per `config.models.plan`. Reproduced as returned; my critique is the next comment.

> **Headline:** the plan is implementable without spec or module-file changes, but COS 3 needs an explicit legacy exception: catalog's shared `CacheControl` component is free-form, so its values cannot be enumerated from OpenAPI. The strongest in-scope solution is to allowlist its five existing operations and reject every new free-form declaration.
>
> Also, the brief is inaccurate at HEAD: catalog's `/openapi.yaml` emits `no-store`, not five minutes.

### Definition of Done
- New package `ticketing/shared/cachetier` defines exactly four tiers: `Never = 0`, `Seconds = 5s`, `Minutes = 5m`, `Hours = 1h`.
- Every tier exposes its `time.Duration`; its header is computed from that duration.
- `Never.CacheControl()` returns `no-store` and remains a registered tier.
- Catalog event, venue, seat-map and price-resolution reads derive their existing named header bindings from the registry; inventory availability and seat-occupancy likewise.
- Every affected response header remains byte-identical.
- A cross-service test parses every `services/*/api/openapi.yaml`, validates every literal `Cache-Control` enum against the registry, rejects new free-form declarations, and explicitly excludes `/openapi.yaml`.
- No caching, tier assignment, OpenAPI, generated-code, module or workspace changes. `make check` passes when invoked alone.

### Design — `shared/go/cachetier`

```go
type Tier time.Duration

const (
    Never   Tier = 0
    Seconds Tier = Tier(5 * time.Second)
    Minutes Tier = Tier(5 * time.Minute)
    Hours   Tier = Tier(time.Hour)
)
```

API: `Duration() time.Duration`, `CacheControl() string`, `All() []Tier`, `FromCacheControl(string) (Tier, bool)`.

`CacheControl` validates the receiver is one of `All()` before rendering: zero duration -> `no-store`; positive registered duration -> `public, max-age=<seconds>, s-maxage=<seconds>`. The numeric duration is therefore the only source of positive TTL text, and an unregistered `Tier` must fail loudly rather than render a fifth tier. `Never` is deliberately a real zero-duration registry entry, so `FromCacheControl("no-store")` returns `(Never, true)` — distinguishable from unknown or missing.

**Existing service identifiers keep their names and call sites.** They must become package *variables* because Go does not permit a function-derived string as a `const`; no HEAD use requires a constant expression.

```go
var CacheControlPublicReads = cachetier.Minutes.CacheControl()
```

Equivalent bindings for venue reads, price resolution, availability and occupancy. `cacheControlForSeatMaps` returns `cachetier.Never.CacheControl()` on both no-store branches; the published branch keeps returning `CacheControlPublicVenueReads`, now derived from `cachetier.Hours`.

**Left alone deliberately:** the generic `writeJSON`/`write` error defaults (general HTTP safety defaults, not public data-tier selection) and every `/openapi.yaml` handler (static contract documents are outside ADR-004 data tiers).

### The OpenAPI audit test

New file `smoke/cachetier_contract_test.go`, in package `smoke_test` alongside the existing cross-service contract tests. It should:

1. Discover `../services/*/api/openapi.yaml` with `filepath.Glob`, avoiding a hand-maintained five-service list.
2. Parse each **source** document with `kin-openapi/openapi3`.
3. Walk paths -> operations -> responses -> response headers named `Cache-Control`.
4. Skip `/openapi.yaml` before inspecting headers, with the reason in the test: *"The served OpenAPI document is a static asset; its TTL is not an ADR-004 data tier."*
5. For an enum-bearing header, require every enum member to be accepted by `cachetier.FromCacheControl`.
6. For a header without an enum, **fail**, except for an explicit legacy table containing exactly `listPublicEvents`, `getPublicEvent`, `getPublicSeason`, `getPublicFestival` (minutes) and `listPublicVenues` (hours). Any sixth operation reusing catalog's free-form component fails. The exception is therefore visible and bounded, not a silent skip.

Parsing the YAML beats inspecting generated Go: OpenAPI is authoritative under ADR-009, header-component enums are not reliably represented in generated models, and four services' specs are not embedded in code the smoke package consumes.

### File-by-file

| File | Status | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `shared/go/cachetier/cachetier.go` | **New** | `Tier`, four durations, rendering, enumeration, lookup |
| `shared/go/cachetier/cachetier_test.go` | **New** | Pin durations, exact bytes, lookup, `Never`, rejection of an unregistered tier |
| `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go` | Existing | Import `cachetier`; derive minutes/hours bindings; `Never` in both seat-map no-store branches. `GetOpenAPISpec` and generic `writeJSON` defaults unchanged |
| `services/catalog/internal/api/pricing.go` | Existing | Derive `CacheControlPriceResolution` from `cachetier.Never` |
| `services/inventory/internal/api/server.go` | Existing | Derive both seconds-tier bindings from `cachetier.Seconds`; static spec route and generic write default unchanged |
| `smoke/cachetier_contract_test.go` | **New** | Cross-service source-spec audit, negative fixtures, free-form allowlist, static-document exclusion |

No changes to `services/*/api/openapi.yaml`, `openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`, any `go.mod`/`go.sum`/`go.work`, or any ADR. Catalog and inventory already consume `ticketing/shared/*` through the workspace; the new package is inside that same module and adds no external dependency, so ADR-035's pattern requires no manifest change.

### Test plan — new tests, observed red first

| Test | Assertion | Initial red |
|---|---|---|
| `TestRegisteredTiers` | Four exact durations; headers exactly `no-store`, 5s, 300s, 3600s; `All()` has no fifth tier | Compile failure — `Tier`, values and methods do not exist |
| `TestFromCacheControl` | All four strings resolve; a 60-second value and malformed strings do not; `no-store` resolves to `Never`, not "not found" | Compile failure — lookup absent |
| `TestUnregisteredTierCannotRender` | A cast duration outside the registry cannot emit an invented header | Fails if a naive renderer formats every positive duration |
| `TestDeclaredCacheControlValuesUseRegisteredTiers` | All current enum literals known; only the five catalog operations may use the legacy free-form component | Compile failure before the registry exists; a synthetic unknown enum proves the traversal reports a real negative |
| `TestCacheControlAuditRejectsNewFreeFormDeclaration` | A synthetic sixth free-form operation fails audit | Fails if the audit silently skips schemas with no enum |
| `TestCacheControlAuditExcludesOpenAPISpecDocument` | A synthetic `/openapi.yaml` static header is excluded categorically | Fails before the path exclusion exists |

### Existing tests — characterization pins, must stay unchanged
`TestSeatMapReadCacheTierByStatus`, `TestResolveTicketTypePrice`, `TestPublicListIsLocalizedAndCacheTiered`, `TestPublicDetail`, `TestFestivalPublicGroupedRead`, `TestListPublicVenues`, `TestAvailabilityCacheTierIsContractEnforced`, `TestSeatOccupancyCacheTierIsContractEnforced`, `TestCatalogPublicationAndStorefront`, `TestSeriesSeasonPublicationAndStorefrontGrouping`, `TestFestivalPublicationSharedCapacityAndPublicGrouping`, `TestBackofficeVenueReadHoursTier`.

### Risks
- Duration conversion could introduce rounding/formatting drift — prevented by accepting only registered whole-second durations and pinning all four complete strings.
- Converting exported constants to variables technically makes them mutable; that is the cost of keeping the identifiers while deriving values through a function.
- ADR-028 makes enum-covered drift an immediate runtime 500; the inventory tests prove it.
- **Catalog's free-form `CacheControl` gets no equivalent ADR-028 value validation.** Exact hard-coded smoke assertions are the independent byte proof there — *tests comparing a handler to the same compatibility binding are not sufficient alone.*
- The spec test's relative path follows the smoke-suite convention; a glob prevents service-list drift.

### Problems in the ticket
1. **The brief's catalog `/openapi.yaml` claim is wrong at HEAD.** `GetOpenAPISpec` emits `no-store`; *inventory* emits the five-minute static value inline. The exclusion should be categorical by route, not tied to a claimed current byte.
2. **COS 3's strongest wording is not fully achievable while OpenAPI changes are forbidden.** Catalog's free-form `CacheControl` declares no values, so no test can enumerate them from the authoritative contract. The bounded allowlist prevents new free-form endpoint classes, but the allowlisted operations still rely on behavioural tests. Removing the exception entirely requires replacing the free-form component with single-valued minutes and hours components — a spec change plus regeneration, explicitly out of scope here.

**Critique by `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)** per `config.models.planReview`. Adversarial pass: every file, symbol and test seam the draft names was checked against HEAD with `git grep -n` before accepting it.

### Verified — accepted as drafted

| Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| All 12 named existing tests exist | **True.** Each resolves at HEAD (`pricing_test.go`, `server_test.go`, `seatmap_test.go`, `availability_cache_tier_test.go`, `smoke/catalog_publication_test.go`, `smoke/backoffice_venue_list_test.go`) |
| Exactly five operations use catalog's free-form `CacheControl` component | **True.** `listPublicEvents`, `getPublicEvent`, `getPublicSeason`, `getPublicFestival`, `listPublicVenues` — verified at `openapi.yaml:889/917/946/972/998`. No sixth |
| Catalog's `/openapi.yaml` emits `no-store`, not the minutes tier | **True, and the draft is correcting my brief.** `server.go:1199`. Inventory is the one emitting `public, max-age=300` inline (`server.go:59`), as are access, commerce and payments. Accepted; the brief was wrong |
| No `go.mod` / `go.work` change needed | **True.** Catalog imports `ticketing/shared/contract` with **no** `require` line — the workspace resolves it. A new package under the same module inherits that, and ADR-035's drift checker reads manifests only, so an unchanged manifest cannot trip it |
| `shared/go` already depends on `kin-openapi v0.142.0` | **True** (`shared/go/go.mod:6`) — matters for amendment 1 below |
| Durations render to today's bytes | **True.** 5s -> `max-age=5`, 5m -> `300`, 1h -> `3600`, 0 -> `no-store`. All four match HEAD byte-for-byte |
| `Never` as a real registered zero-duration tier | **Accepted.** Making `no-store` a tier rather than an absence is what lets the audit distinguish "declared never" from "declared nothing" — that distinction is load-bearing for COS 5 |
| Exported constants become package `var`s | **Accepted.** Go cannot make a function-derived string a `const`, and no call site needs a constant expression. The mutability is theoretical; ADR-028 catches the consequence at runtime anyway |

### Amendment 1 — **BLOCKING**: the audit test must not live in `smoke`

The draft puts `TestDeclaredCacheControlValuesUseRegisteredTiers` and its two negative fixtures in package `smoke_test`. That placement is wrong for this test, and the reason is mechanical rather than stylistic:

- `Makefile:6` — `GO_TEST_MODULES := $(filter-out smoke,$(GO_MODULES))`. **`make test-go` does not run the smoke module at all.**
- The smoke module only runs via `make smoke` -> `scripts/smoke.sh`, which boots an isolated Docker Compose stack (six services, Postgres, NATS, per-checkout port slots) and *then* runs `go test -tags smoke ./...`.

So a **static YAML-parsing test that needs no stack whatsoever** would (a) not run in the fast Go loop, (b) require Docker to execute at all, and (c) be unable to fail for its own reasons without the whole stack being up first. That is the slowest possible feedback for the cheapest possible check, and it also lands the test inside `smoke/coverage_test.go`'s `TestMain` gate, which has its own filtered-run semantics.

**Amended placement:** `shared/go/cachetier/spec_audit_test.go`, globbing `../../../services/*/api/openapi.yaml`.

- `shared/go` is in `GO_TEST_MODULES`, so it runs in `make test-go` — seconds, no Docker.
- It already has `kin-openapi`, so no dependency is added and ADR-035's drift check stays untouched.
- No import of any service package: the test reads the spec **files**, so the module dependency direction is not inverted. Only the filesystem is crossed, and only in a `_test.go` file.
- The audit sits in the same package as the registry it enforces, which is where a future reader will look for it.

**Required with it:** the glob must assert it found the expected number of service specs (five at HEAD). A relative path that silently matches zero files is exactly the "test that cannot fail" this repo has a named learning about (`docs/learnings/2026-08-03-a-fixture-too-small-cannot-show-the-negative.md`); the count guard turns path fragility into a loud failure, and makes a sixth service an explicit decision rather than a silent omission.

### Amendment 2 — the draft's own risk note is right, and it upgrades one test to load-bearing

The draft observes, correctly, that *"tests comparing a handler to the same compatibility binding are not sufficient alone."* I checked how far that reaches, because it decides whether COS 2 is actually proven:

- **Inventory and price resolution are safe without any new test.** Their spec declarations are single-valued `enum`s, so ADR-028's response validator turns a drifted byte into a 500 — `TestAvailabilityCacheTierIsContractEnforced` and `TestSeatOccupancyCacheTierIsContractEnforced` fail *because of the contract*, not because of the constant they compare to.
- **Seat maps and venues are safe.** `TestSeatMapReadCacheTierByStatus` uses a literal (`hoursTier := "public, max-age=3600, s-maxage=3600"`), as does `smoke/backoffice_venue_list_test.go:43`.
- **Catalog's minutes tier is the gap.** `server_test.go:1669/1741/1954` all compare against `CacheControlPublicReads` itself — self-referential, and the free-form component means ADR-028 cannot help. The only literal pin is `smoke/catalog_publication_test.go:202`, in the **stack-gated** suite.

Consequence: if the registry rendered `public, max-age=300` (no `s-maxage`), catalog's own `go test ./...` would pass and only the Docker smoke stage would catch it. That is not a hole in `make check` — the smoke stage is part of it — but it is a slow, expensive place to learn about a one-character bug.

**This is what makes `TestRegisteredTiers` load-bearing rather than a formality:** it pins all four complete strings as literals, in the fast loop, at the single point they are now generated. It is not a tautology test and must not be written as one — it must assert the four literal strings, never `Minutes.CacheControl() == Minutes.CacheControl()` or a re-derivation of the same format expression.

### Amendment 3 — negative fixtures must be synthetic in-test documents

The draft implies but does not state it. `TestCacheControlAuditRejectsNewFreeFormDeclaration` and `TestCacheControlAuditExcludesOpenAPISpecDocument` must build their spec documents **in the test**, never by mutating a repo `openapi.yaml`. A negative fixture that edits a tracked file would either fail `check-generate` or leave the tree dirty. The audit logic therefore has to be a function taking a parsed document, with the file-walking loop as its only caller.

### Amendment 4 — pin the fail-loud mode of `CacheControl()`

The draft says an unregistered `Tier` "must fail loudly" without saying how. **Panic**, and document why it is safe: every call site is a package-level `var` initializer, so an unregistered tier is a process-start failure, not a request-path panic. `TestUnregisteredTierCannotRender` asserts the panic rather than a sentinel return — a sentinel would let a caller ignore it and emit an empty `Cache-Control`, which ADR-028 would then turn into a 500 on a *public read* instead of a loud boot failure.

### Rejected — nothing

No part of the draft is rejected. Amendments 1 and 4 change *where* and *how*; 2 and 3 tighten claims the draft already made.

### Pre-mortem — it is three weeks later and this ticket caused an incident. What happened?

1. **A public read started returning 500s.** Cause: a tier value drifted against an ADR-028 single-value enum. *Guarded:* the two inventory contract tests and the price-resolution enum fail closed on exactly this, and `TestRegisteredTiers` pins the bytes upstream of them.
2. **A shared cache started serving events for an hour.** Cause: someone assigned the wrong tier. *Not guarded, and out of scope:* this ticket changes no tier assignment. The audit test proves a value is a *known tier*, never that it is the *right* tier for that endpoint. Say so in the test's doc comment so a future reader does not over-trust it.
3. **The audit test silently stopped auditing.** Cause: the repo layout moved and the glob matched nothing. *Guarded by amendment 1's count assertion.* This is the most likely of the three and the cheapest to prevent.
4. **A new endpoint shipped with an undeclared tier.** *Partly guarded:* the audit constrains what is **declared**, not what is **emitted**. An endpoint that emits a header and declares nothing is invisible to it — that is the exact TKT-128 defect, and it stays open after this ticket. Name it in the plan-final rather than letting the registry imply coverage it does not have.

**The `kind=plan` draft as amended below is the plan.** Delta only — the draft is not restated.

### Amendments carried from plan-review (all four, unchanged)

1. **[blocking]** The audit test moves from `smoke/cachetier_contract_test.go` to `shared/go/cachetier/spec_audit_test.go`, globbing `../../../services/*/api/openapi.yaml`, **with an assertion that the glob found five specs**. Reason: `smoke` is filtered out of `GO_TEST_MODULES` and only runs behind a Docker Compose stack.
2. `TestRegisteredTiers` pins all four **literal** header strings — it is the byte proof for catalog's minutes tier, which is otherwise only compared against itself in the fast loop.
3. The two audit negative fixtures build **synthetic in-test spec documents**; the audit logic is a function over a parsed document, and the file walk is its only caller.
4. `CacheControl()` **panics** on an unregistered `Tier`; `TestUnregisteredTierCannotRender` asserts the panic, not a sentinel.

### Decisions made by the agent under the waived Gate 2

The repo owner waived plan approval for this run. Rule applied: prefer the option the critique recommends; where it makes none, take the most reversible. Both open decisions are recorded here with the reasoning that would otherwise have been the owner's.

**Decision 1 — catalog's free-form `CacheControl` component: allowlist the five operations; do NOT change the spec.**

The draft named the alternative honestly: replace the free-form component with single-valued minutes and hours components, which would close the exception completely and, through ADR-028, make a drifted byte on catalog's four public reads fail closed the way inventory's already does. That is a better end state.

Chosen anyway, for three reasons that agree:
- The critique recommends it ("the strongest **in-scope** solution").
- It is the more reversible option. An allowlist is deleted in one commit; an enum-tightened spec is a published contract change plus regenerated `openapi_gen.go`.
- **It is the only option that keeps this ticket's central promise.** Tightening the enum makes a drifted `Cache-Control` a runtime 500 on four public reads. That is a behaviour change, and this ticket's whole claim — the one that lets it carry `risk:low` — is that nothing observable changes. Smuggling a fail-closed behaviour change into a "no behaviour change" prefactor is exactly how a low-risk label stops meaning anything.

**Carved out to a follow-up ticket** (to be created at closeout, not left implicit): tighten catalog's `CacheControl` component into single-valued `PublicMinutesCacheControl` / `PublicHoursCacheControl` components, deleting the allowlist and extending ADR-028's fail-closed coverage to catalog's four public reads. That ticket owns the behaviour change and the regeneration; this one does not.

**Decision 2 — audit test placement (amendment 1) overrides the draft.**

Not a preference. `Makefile:6` excludes `smoke` from `make test-go`, and `scripts/smoke.sh` boots a full Compose stack before running it. A test that parses YAML files and touches no service would have been unable to run without Docker. Most-reversible also favours it: a test file moves between packages in one commit.

### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

Per the skill's requirement — these reached Gate 2 authored by the reviewer and critiqued by nobody. Under a waived gate they are the items most worth the owner's eye, because the cross-model guarantee does not cover them:

1. **The move of the audit test to `shared/go/cachetier` and the five-spec count guard** (amendment 1). Wholly mine. The mechanical facts behind it are verified (`Makefile:6`, `scripts/smoke.sh`, `shared/go/go.mod:6`), but the *choice* of `shared/go/cachetier` over, say, a `gateway` or a new module is a judgement no second model saw. Concretely: it puts a test that reads service specs inside the shared module. No import direction is inverted — the filesystem is crossed, not the module graph — but a reader could reasonably call it a layering smell.
2. **`CacheControl()` panicking rather than returning a sentinel** (amendment 4). Mine. Safe today because every call site is a package-level initializer; it stops being safe the moment a future caller computes a tier at request time. Guarded only by a doc comment.
3. **The requirement that `TestRegisteredTiers` assert literal strings and not re-derive the format** (amendment 2). Mine, and the whole byte-identity proof in the fast loop rests on it.

### What this ticket does NOT guarantee — stated so the registry does not imply coverage it lacks

- The audit proves a declared value is a **known tier**. It never proves it is the **right** tier for that endpoint. Tier assignment is unchanged by this ticket and unchecked by it.
- The audit constrains what is **declared**, not what is **emitted**. An endpoint that emits a `Cache-Control` and declares nothing stays invisible — that is precisely the TKT-128 defect class, and it remains open after this ticket. Both sentences go into the audit test's doc comment.

### `risk:low` — re-verified against the final plan
Six files (2 new, 4 touched — one of them the new test), no spec change, no regeneration, no migration, no auth, no money path, no CI config. Under the five-file guidance and inside every carve-out. Label stands.

**Gate 2 waived by the repo owner; the agent proceeds to Building.**

**Implemented by `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)** per `config.models.implement`. TDD, plan-final followed with no deviations.

```yaml
stage: coding
implementer: main-agent (Claude Opus 5)
branch: TKT-204-ttl-tier-registry
commit: 14acb383
pr: https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/168
gate: make check — EXIT=0, log body clean (no "Error N", "FAIL", "drifted")
files: 2 new, 3 modified
spec_change: none
regeneration: none
```

### TDD — red observed before every line of implementation

`cachetier_test.go` was written first and run: **build failure**, `undefined: Tier / Never / Seconds / Minutes / Hours / All`. Only then was `cachetier.go` written.

Finding 3 is the one worth pausing on: my own change put the call on a request path, and my own doc comment asserted it had not. Those receivers were registered constants and could never have panicked — but the stated invariant was false, and a false invariant in a comment is how the next person gets it wrong.

**Partially rejected, with reason:** finding 3's *recommendation* was to make `Tier` opaque or split `CacheControl()` into `(string, error)` plus a `MustCacheControl`. Rejected as more API than the risk removes, for a package with four constants and no computed-tier caller. The **substance** was fixed (no `cachetier` call remains on a request path) and the API contract is now written down, including the rule for the caller that would change the answer.

### Pass 2 — base `14acb383` (fix diff 1): 1 finding, [medium], real, fixed

The 2xx scoping I introduced in pass 1's fix was too broad a narrowing: removing `NeverCacheControl` from `authenticateStaff`'s 401, or from the shared `StaffWriteUnauthorized` response, changed nothing and raised nothing. Those *are* tier decisions — a `no-store` on a credential-validity answer is the contract saying that response is never shared-cacheable.

**CONFIRMED → fixed.** The exclusion is now about repetition rather than status: every 2xx and every **inline** non-2xx is pinned; a `$ref` inheritance is pinned once at its shared component. Catalog's twenty-odd staff writes cost one line, and deleting the header from the component they share fails. Verified inline-vs-shared against the spec directly (`authenticateStaff` 401 is inline at `openapi.yaml:849`; `StaffWriteUnauthorized` is the component at `:1212`).

**This pass invalidated pass 1's fix at the root, which resets the churn counter** (skill § second pass, absolute cap 4) — that is why a third pass ran.

### Pass 3 — base `57301541` (fix diff 2): 1 finding, [high], real, fixed differently than recommended

`auditSpec` walks only operations under `doc.Paths`, so a `Cache-Control` declared inside a **callback** would never enter the pinned set and could later be deleted unnoticed.

**CONFIRMED, and the preconditions checked before acting:**
- `grep -nE "^\s*(callbacks|webhooks):" services/*/api/openapi.yaml` → **none**.
- Every spec is `openapi: 3.0.3`. **Webhooks are a 3.1 construct and cannot be expressed in these documents at all**, so that half of the finding is unreachable by the document version, not merely by current content.
- No `components.responses` entry is itself a bare `$ref`, so the chained-reference variant does not occur either.

**Fixed by refusal rather than traversal**, departing from the recommendation. Adding callback/webhook traversal now would mean shipping walk code that **no committed document exercises** — untested machinery guarding a case that does not occur, which is its own way to be wrong. Instead the audit *refuses* a document declaring either, naming `auditSpec` as the thing to extend. The gap becomes a loud failure the moment it is first reachable, and whoever hits it will have a real document to test the traversal against. Mutation-checked both ways, including by adding a callback to the **real** catalog spec.
